content.overview: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Part III rights and empowers the Court to issue directions, orders or writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto. The right cannot be suspended except as the Constitution provides. Article 226 is the High Court power to issue those writs for fundamental rights and for any other purpose. Article 32 is itself a fundamental right. Article 226 is not in Part III. This topic is the remedy; the petition-format subject covers drafting and was not reopened.
content.study: Use Article 32 only for a Part III right in the Supreme Court. Use Article 226 in the High Court, including for other purposes. Name the writ that matches the relief.

sections.heading: Art 32 vs Art 226
sections.body: Prefer 226 for territorial convenience or non-FR public-law wrongs; use 32 for Part III in the Supreme Court.

enhancement.definition: Article 32 is the Supreme Court enforcement right for Part III. Article 226 is the High Court's wider writ power.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A remedy needs a Part III right for Article 32. Article 226 can also enforce other legal rights. Suspension is only as the Constitution provides.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India, Articles 32 and 226. Emergency suspension is Articles 359 and related provisions and is not restated as a holding.
essentialIngredients: Supreme Court or High Court correctly chosen
Article 226 other-purpose plea only in the High Court
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 32(1) is the right to move the Supreme Court. Article 32(2) lists the writs. Article 32(3) allows Parliament to empower other courts. Article 32(4) bars suspension except as provided. Habeas corpus tests custody. Mandamus commands a public duty. Prohibition and certiorari control jurisdictional error. Quo warranto tests title to a public office. Article 226 repeats the writ power for fundamental rights and adds any other purpose, with territorial limits in the article. A Part IV-only claim does not become Article 32 because the petitioner wants a writ.
examples: A Part III arrest violation is taken to the Supreme Court under Article 32 in habeas corpus.
A statutory licence duty is enforced in the High Court under Article 226.
A Directive Principle alone is filed under Article 32. Article 37, not Article 32, answers that claim.
enhancement.problemApplication: Name the right, the court and the writ. If the right is not in Part III, Article 32 is the wrong article.

It enforces Part III, not Part IV.
The five writs are named in the article.
Article 226 is wider and is not in Part III.
